Arcs and chords: A circle is the set of points at a fixed distance (the radius) from a center. A chord joins two points on the circle and the diameter is the longest chord. A central angle has its vertex at the center and its measure equals the measure of its intercepted arc. Arcs are minor, major or semicircles, and arcs of congruent circles are congruent when their central angles are. A radius perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord, and congruent chords are the same distance from the center.
Inscribed angles: An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle and its sides are chords. Its measure is half the measure of its intercepted arc. Inscribed angles that intercept the same arc are congruent, an angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle, and opposite angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle are supplementary. Angles formed by two chords inside the circle equal half the sum of the intercepted arcs.
Tangents and secants: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point and is perpendicular to the radius at that point. Two tangents from the same outside point are congruent. A secant crosses the circle at two points. Angles formed outside the circle equal half the difference of the intercepted arcs. For lengths: when two secants (or a secant and a tangent) come from one outside point, the product of the whole secant and its outside part is the same for both, and for a tangent the square of its length equals that product.
Arc length and sector area: Arc length is a fraction of the circumference: arc length = (central angle / 360) x 2 x pi x r. Sector area is the same fraction of the circle's area: sector area = (central angle / 360) x pi x r^2. If the angle is in radians, arc length = r x theta and area = one half x r^2 x theta. A segment is the region between a chord and an arc, and its area is the sector area minus the triangle area.
Equation of a circle: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has the equation (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2. If the center is the origin, x^2 + y^2 = r^2. To find the center and radius from a general equation, complete the square in x and y. A point is inside, on or outside the circle depending on whether its squared distance from the center is less than, equal to or greater than r^2.
